tenXCollapse.statement: At 10x BOTH builds collapse, so the transaction-id hold is the only 10x figure that separates them. Of 7,165 events offered in the window base committed 185 and head 192, that is 2.6 and 2.7 percent, with 7,036 and 7,062 transport errors (client timeouts) and zero non-2xx on either side; base's live frames from the write's response read 0.0/0.0 because almost nothing was delivered in time to measure.
tenXCollapse.whatNotToRead: On that collapsed step head's write latency reads worse than base's (comment write_ms p50/p99 10957.5/15232.5 against 6749.3/8808.6, anchored 17217.0/23478.5 against 16186.0/17219.8) and its Dispatch RSS max reads 2,121.4 MiB against 1,790.4. Neither is a comparison: both are taken over the few requests and the few seconds that survived two saturated runs on a 2-CPU pod, and 10x offers ten times what this stack can serve. I would not read the 18 percent RSS difference as a regression without a step that does not saturate; at 1x, which does not, head's RSS is lower than base's (2,719.7 against 2,828.5 MiB). The hold is sampled from pg_stat_activity rather than bound by the offered rate, which is why it still separates the builds at 10x.
tenXCollapse.boxBusyBefore: At 1x at most 3.4 percent. At 10x up to 81 percent, because the previous 10x step's own drain overlaps the reading that run-step.sh takes before its reset; that is the harness measuring its own predecessor, not other work of mine, and no step of mine ran beside another.
